provenance.evaluator: Second Run campaign (compiled from campaign/README.md Run 1 arm B, availability/observations.jsonl and availability/README.md API-source notes, 2026-09-23/24)
provenance.account_used: new DigitalOcean account created for the Second Run campaign; started Tier 2 with GPU Droplet limit 0
provenance.disclosure: DigitalOcean arm self-funded at list price ($4.41/GPU-hr H100); no credit, partnership or discount from DigitalOcean. modeled_cost_usd is the historical estimate for Run 1 arm B (~55 min wall clock); the posted invoice line was not independently reconciled.

account_creation.notes: New accounts start Tier 2 with GPU Droplet limit 0; a support ticket raised the limit to 1 in under a day (known campaign fact). That matches quota_gate=soft: self-serve sign-up plus a ticket, not a sales conversation. Exact wall-clock time from starting sign-up to placing the ticket, and from account creation to the ticket being raised, were not recorded precisely (only 'under a day' for the ticket).

price_transparency.minimum_billing: 5 minutes (pricing page) vs 60 seconds (docs) -- the two DigitalOcean sources disagree
price_transparency.notes: Primary reference SKU is gpu-h100x1-base at $4.41/GPU-hr, per-second billing, published on the public pricing page without login. MI300X (gpu-amd-base) was $2.59/GPU-hr in providers/PROVIDERS.md staging. Per-second billing is documented, but the minimum-billing window itself is inconsistent between the pricing page and the docs -- recorded, not resolved.

provisioning.notes: No timed request-to-SSH provisioning attempt for this shop-eval lane exists in prior sessions. Run 1 arm B did reach SSH (see availability_honesty: time_to_ssh_s 60 on 2026-09-23T17:49:00Z) but that figure lives in the ledger as an availability observation, not a dedicated 3x-timed provisioning attempt for this record; a fresh counter run should time 3 creates directly.

availability_honesty.notes: All 14 digitalocean rows in availability/observations.jsonl as of 2026-09-24. Only the first (Run 1 arm B, droplet 603084148, nyc2 gpu-h100x1-80gb) is a real delivered create; the rest are console or API listings (console-plan-list, api). H200 was out of capacity in all 6 regions checked on 2026-09-23. MI300X was greyed out / out_of_capacity in NYC2 and TOR1 at plan-list time; the 2026-09-24 API sample also reported gpu-mi300x1-192gb out_of_capacity globally. The 2026-09-23T19:14:00Z row records a create that was never completed because the browser froze -- recorded as available/not-provisioned, arm skipped, not as a provider failure.

api_cli_tui_quality.notes: doctl authenticated with a self-serve API token; `doctl compute size list` performs list_op. create_op observed true through the console (Run 1 arm B). Droplet deletion after Run 1 was instructed by the campaign runbook but no confirmation of the delete call itself was captured in these sessions, so delete_op is unobserved rather than assumed. The console needed a manual reload to reflect current state after a create/list action (known campaign fact) -- a UI-quality defect, not a data field in this schema, recorded here.

billing_granularity.billing_quantum: per-second billing; minimum window disputed between the pricing page (5 minutes) and the docs (60 seconds)
billing_granularity.notes: The billing quantum itself is known from public sources, but no prior session checked account balance or an invoice line before and after a delete to confirm billing actually stopped at delete time.

tenant_hygiene.notes: Not checked in any prior session.

network_path.notes: Not checked in any prior session; Run 1 arm B's droplet IP was collected for the runner (`collect.sh do-h100 root@<ip-B>`) but firewall defaults and a first-boot port scan were never recorded.

support_path.notes: A support ticket to raise the GPU Droplet quota from 0 to 1 took under a day (known campaign fact); the exact response time in seconds was not recorded. No sales conversation was required.

termination.notes: The campaign runbook instructs deleting each droplet after its arm completes, but no prior session recorded the delete method used or confirmed billing stopped for the DigitalOcean side.
